plan: Genesis 7:1-24; Genesis 8:1-22; Genesis 9:1-17, 18–10:1; Genesis 10:2-5; 1 Chronicles 1:5-7; Genesis 10:6-20; 1 Chronicles 1:8-16; Genesis 10:21-30; 1 Chronicles 1:17-23; Genesis 10:31-32

readings.title: Entering the Ark
readings.subtitle: The Waters Prevail
readings.text:
[Genesis 7:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Noaḥ, <dq>“Come into the ark, you and all your household, because <dn>I</dn> have seen that you are righteous before <dn>Me</dn> in this generation.</dq>
[2] <dq>“Of all the clean beasts take with you seven pairs, a male and his female; and of the beasts that are unclean two, a male and his female;</dq>
[3] <dq>and of birds of the heavens seven pairs, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the face of all the earth.</dq>
[4] <dq>“For after seven more days <dn>I</dn> am sending rain on the earth, forty days and forty nights, and shall wipe from the face of the earth <dn>את</dn> all that stand that <dn>I</dn> created.”</dq>
[5] And Noaḥ did according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded him.
[6] Now Noaḥ was six hundred years old when the flood-waters were on the earth.
[7] And Noaḥ and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives went into the ark because of the waters of the flood.
[8] Of the clean beasts and of the beasts that are unclean, and of birds, and of all that creep on the earth,
[9] two by two they went into the ark to Noaḥ, male and female, as <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded Noaḥ.
[10] And it came to be after seven days that the waters of the flood were on the earth.
[11] In the six hundredth year of Noaḥ’s life, in the second new moon, the seventeenth day of the moon, on that day all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
[12] And the rain was on the earth forty days and forty nights.
[13] On that same day Noaḥ and Shěm and Ḥam and Yapheth, the sons of Noaḥ, and Noaḥ’s wife and the three wives of his sons with <dn>את</dn> them, went into the ark,
[14] they and every life form after its kind, and every beast after its kind, and every creeping creature that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.
[15] And they went into the ark to Noaḥ, two by two, of all flesh in which is the breath of life.
[16] And those going in, male and female of all flesh, went in as <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded him, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shut him in.
[17] And the flood was on the earth forty days, and the waters increased and lifted up <dn>את</dn> the ark, and it rose high above the earth.
[18] And the waters were mighty and greatly increased on the earth, and the ark moved about on the surface of the waters.
[19] And the waters were exceedingly mighty on the earth, and all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.
[20] The waters became mighty, fifteen cubits upward, and the mountains were covered.
[21] And all flesh died – the creeping creature on the earth – birds and cattle and beasts and every swarming creature that swarms on the earth, and all mankind.
[22] All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, all that was on the dry land, died.
[23] So <dn>He</dn> wiped off <dn>את</dn> all that stand, which were on the face of the ground – both man and beast, creeping creature and bird of the heavens. And they were wiped off from the earth. And only Noaḥ was left, and those with <dn>את</dn> him in the ark.
[24] And the waters were mighty on the earth, one hundred and fifty days.

readings.title: The Ark Rests
readings.subtitle: The Covenant of Seasons
readings.text:
[Genesis 8:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> remembered <dn>את</dn> Noaḥ, and <dn>את</dn> all the beasts and <dn>את</dn> all the cattle that were with <dn>את</dn> him in the ark. And <dn>Elohim</dn> made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
[2] And the fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were stopped, and the rain from the heavens was withheld.
[3] And the waters receded steadily from the earth, and at the end of the hundred and fifty days the waters diminished.
[4] And in the seventh new moon, the seventeenth day of the new moon, the ark rested on the mountains of Ararat.
[5] And the waters decreased steadily until the tenth new moon. In the tenth new moon, on the first day of the new moon, the tops of the mountains became visible.
[6] And it came to be, at the end of forty days, that Noaḥ opened <dn>את</dn> the window of the ark which he had made,
[7] and he sent out <dn>את</dn> a raven, which kept going out and turning back until the waters had dried up from the earth.
[8] Then he sent out <dn>את</dn> a dove from <dn>את</dn> him, to see if the waters had receded from the face of the ground.
[9] But the dove found no resting place for its feet and returned into the ark to him, for the waters were on the face of all the earth. So he put out his hand and took it, and pulled it into the ark to himself.
[10] And he waited yet another seven days, and again he sent <dn>את</dn> the dove out from the ark.
[11] And the dove came to him in the evening, and see, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in its mouth. And Noaḥ knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
[12] And he waited yet another seven days and sent out <dn>את</dn> the dove, which did not return to him again.
[13] And it came to be in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the new moon, that the waters were dried up from the earth. And Noaḥ removed <dn>את</dn> the covering of the ark and looked, and saw the surface of the ground was dry.
[14] And in the second new moon, on the twenty-seventh day of the new moon, the earth was dry.
[15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to Noaḥ, saying,
[16] <dq>“Go out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons’ wives with <dn>את</dn> you.</dq>
[17] <dq>“Bring out with you every life form of all flesh that is with <dn>את</dn> you: of birds, of cattle and all creeping creatures – the creeping creatures on the earth. And let them teem on the earth, and bear and increase on the earth.”</dq>
[18] So Noaḥ went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with <dn>את</dn> him,
[19] every beast, every creeping creature, and every bird, whatever creeps on the earth, according to their kinds, went out of the ark.
[20] And Noaḥ built a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and took of every clean beast and of every clean bird, and offered ascending offerings on the slaughter-place.
[21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smelled <dn>את</dn> a soothing fragrance, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said in <dn>His</dn> heart, <dq>“Never again shall <dn>I</dn> curse <dn>את</dn> the ground because of man, although the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth, and never again strike <dn>את</dn> all living creatures, as <dn>I</dn> have done,</dq>
[22] <dq>as long as the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.”</dq>

readings.title: The Rainbow Sign
readings.subtitle: The Sanctity of Blood
readings.text:
[Genesis 9:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> Noaḥ and <dn>את</dn> his sons, and said to them, <dq>“Be fruitful and increase, and fill <dn>את</dn> the earth.</dq>
[2] <dq>“And the fear of you and the dread of you is on every beast of the earth, on every bird of the heavens, on all that creeps on the ground, and on all the fish of the sea – into your hand they have been given.</dq>
[3] <dq>“Every creeping creature that lives is food for you. <dn>I</dn> have given you <dn>את</dn> all, as <dn>I</dn> gave the green plants.</dq>
[4] <dq>“But do not eat flesh with its life, its blood.</dq>
[5] <dq>“But only <dn>את</dn> your blood for your lives <dn>I</dn> require, from the hand of every beast <dn>I</dn> require it, and from the hand of man. From the hand of every man’s brother <dn>I</dn> require <dn>את</dn> the life of man.</dq>
[6] <dq>“Whoever sheds man’s blood, by man his blood is shed, for in the image of <dn>Elohim</dn> has <dn>He</dn> made <dn>את</dn> man.</dq>
[7] <dq>“As for you, be fruitful and increase, bring forth teemingly in the earth and increase in it.”</dq>
[8] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to Noaḥ and to his sons with <dn>את</dn> him, saying,
[9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn>, see, <dn>I</dn> establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> you and with <dn>את</dn> your seed after you,</dq>
[10] <dq>and with <dn>את</dn> every living being that is with <dn>את</dn> you: of the birds, of the cattle, and of every beast of the earth with <dn>את</dn> you, of all that go out of the ark, every beast of the earth.</dq>
[11] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> you, and never again is all flesh cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again is there a flood to destroy the earth.”</dq>
[12] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“This is the sign of the covenant which <dn>I</dn> make between <dn>Me</dn> and you, and every living being that is with <dn>את</dn> you, for all generations to come:</dq>
[13] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> rainbow in the cloud, and it shall be for the sign of the covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and the earth.</dq>
[14] <dq>“And it shall be, when <dn>I</dn> bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow shall be seen in the cloud,</dq>
[15] <dq>and <dn>I</dn> shall remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant which is between <dn>Me</dn> and you and every living being of all flesh, and never again let the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh.</dq>
[16] <dq>“And the rainbow shall be in the cloud, and <dn>I</dn> shall see it, to remember the everlasting covenant between <dn>Elohim</dn> and every living being of all flesh that is on the earth.”</dq>
[17] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Noaḥ, <dq>“This is the sign of the covenant which <dn>I</dn> have established between <dn>Me</dn> and all flesh that is on the earth.”</dq>

readings.title: Noah's Vineyard
readings.subtitle: The Curse of Canaan
readings.text:
[Genesis 9:18] And the sons of Noaḥ who went out of the ark were Shěm and Ḥam and Yapheth. And Ḥam was the father of Kena‛an.
[19] These three were the sons of Noaḥ, and all the earth was overspread from them.
[20] And Noaḥ, a man of the soil, began and planted a vineyard.
[21] And he drank of the wine and was drunk, and became uncovered in his tent.
[22] And Ḥam, the father of Kena‛an, saw <dn>את</dn> the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.
[23] So Shěm and Yapheth took <dn>את</dn> a garment, laid it on both their shoulders, and went backward and covered <dn>את</dn> the nakedness of their father, but their faces were turned away, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.
[24] And Noaḥ awoke from his wine, and he knew <dn>את</dn> what his younger son had done to him,
[25] and he said, “Cursed is Kena‛an, let him become a servant of servants to his brothers.”
[26] And he said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Shěm, and let Kena‛an become his servant.
[27] “Let <dn>Elohim</dn> enlarge Yapheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shěm. And let Kena‛an become his servant.”
[28] And Noaḥ lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
[29] So all the days of Noaḥ were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
[Genesis 10:1] And this is the genealogy of the sons of Noaḥ: Shěm, Ḥam, and Yapheth. And sons were born to them after the flood.

readings.title: The Coastland Peoples
readings.subtitle: The Sons of Gomer and Javan
readings.text:
[Genesis 10:2] The sons of Yapheth: Gomer, and Maḡoḡ, and Maḏai, and Yavan, and Tuḇal, and Mesheḵ, and Tiras.
[3] And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Toḡarmah.
[4] And the sons of Yavan: Elishah and Tarshish, Kittim and Doḏanim.
[5] From these the coastland peoples of the nations were separated into their lands, everyone according to his language, according to their clans, into their nations.
[1 Chronicles 1:5] The sons of Yapheth: Gomer, and Maḡoḡ, and Maḏai, and Yavan, and Tuḇal, and Mesheḵ, and Tiras.
[6] And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Diphath, and Toḡarmah.
[7] And the sons of Yavan: Elishah and Tarshishah, Kittim and Roḏanim.

readings.title: Nimrod and Babel
readings.subtitle: The Canaanite Clans
readings.text:
[Genesis 10:6] And the sons of Ḥam: Kush, and Mitsrayim, and Put, and Kena‛an.
[7] And the sons of Kush: Seḇa, and Ḥavilah, and Saḇtah, and Ra‛mah, and Saḇteḵa. And the sons of Ra‛mah: Sheḇa and Deḏan.
[8] And Kush brought forth <dn>את</dn> Nimroḏ, he began to be a mighty one on the earth.
[9] He was a mighty hunter before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, therefore it is said, “Like Nimroḏ the mighty hunter before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
[10] And the beginning of his reign was Baḇel, and Ereḵ, and Akkaḏ, and Kalněh, in the land of Shin‛ar.
[11] From that land he went to Ashshur and built <dn>את</dn> Ninevěh, and <dn>את</dn> Reḥoḇoth Ir, and <dn>את</dn> Kelaḥ,
[12] and <dn>את</dn> Resen between Ninevěh and Kelaḥ, the great city.
[13] And Mitsrayim brought forth <dn>את</dn> Luḏim, and <dn>את</dn> Anamim, and <dn>את</dn> Lehaḇim, and <dn>את</dn> Naphtuḥim,
[14] and <dn>את</dn> Pathrusim, and <dn>את</dn> Kasluḥim, from whom came the Philistines and Kaphtorim.
[15] And Kena‛an brought forth <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏon his first-born, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥěth,
[16] and <dn>את</dn> the Yeḇusite, and <dn>את</dn> the Amorite, and <dn>את</dn> the Girgashite,
[17] and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥivvite, and <dn>את</dn> the Arite, and <dn>את</dn> the Sinite,
[18] and <dn>את</dn> the Arvaḏite, and <dn>את</dn> the Tsemarite, and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥamathite. And afterward the clans of the Kena‛anites were spread abroad.
[19] And the border of the Kena‛anites was from Tsiḏon as you go toward Gerar, as far as Azzah, as you go toward Seḏom, and Amorah, and Aḏmah, and Tseḇoyim, as far as Lasha.
[20] These were the sons of Ḥam, according to their clans, according to their languages, in their lands, in their nations.
[1 Chronicles 1:8] The sons of Ḥam: Kush and Mitsrayim, Put and Kena‛an.
[9] And the sons of Kush: Seḇa, and Ḥavilah, and Saḇta, and Ra‛mah, and Saḇteḵa. And the sons of Ra‛mah: Sheḇa and Deḏan.
[10] And Kush brought forth <dn>את</dn> Nimroḏ; he began to be a mighty one on the earth.
[11] And Mitsrayim brought forth <dn>את</dn> the Luḏim, and <dn>את</dn> the Anamim, and <dn>את</dn> the Lehaḇim, and <dn>את</dn> the Naphtuḥim,
[12] and <dn>את</dn> the Pathrusim, and <dn>את</dn> the Kasluḥim from whom came the Philistines, and <dn>את</dn> the Kaphtorim.
[13] And Kena‛an brought forth <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏon, his first-born, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥěth,
[14] and <dn>את</dn> the Yeḇusite, and <dn>את</dn> the Amorite, and <dn>את</dn> the Girgashite,
[15] and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥivvite, and <dn>את</dn> the Arqite, and <dn>את</dn> the Sinite,
[16] and <dn>את</dn> the Arvaḏite, and <dn>את</dn> the Tsemarite, and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥamathite.

readings.title: The Line of Eber
readings.subtitle: The Division of the Earth
readings.text:
[Genesis 10:21] And also to Shěm, the father of all the children of Ěḇer, the brother of Yapheth the elder, children were born.
[22] The sons of Shěm: Ěylam, and Asshur, and Arpaḵshaḏ, and Luḏ, and Aram.
[23] And the sons of Aram: Uts, and Ḥul, and Gether, and Mash.
[24] And Arpaḵshaḏ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Shelaḥ, and Shelaḥ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ěḇer.
[25] And to Ěḇer were born two sons, the name of one was Peleḡ, for in his days the earth was divided, and his brother’s name was Yoqtan.
[26] And Yoqtan brought forth <dn>את</dn> Almoḏaḏ, and <dn>את</dn> Sheleph, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥatsarmaveth, and <dn>את</dn> Yeraḥ,
[27] and <dn>את</dn> Haḏoram, and <dn>את</dn> Uzal, and <dn>את</dn> Diqlah,
[28] and <dn>את</dn> Oḇal, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇima’ěl, and <dn>את</dn> Sheḇa,
[29] and <dn>את</dn> Ophir, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥavilah, and <dn>את</dn> Yoḇaḇ. All these were sons of Yoqtan.
[30] And their dwelling place was from Měysha as you go toward Sephar, a mountain of the east.
[1 Chronicles 1:17] The sons of Shěm: Ěylam, and Asshur, and Arpaḵshaḏ, and Luḏ, and Aram, and Uts, Ḥul, and Gether, and Mesheḵ.
[18] And Arpaḵshaḏ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Shelaḥ, and Shelaḥ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ěḇer.
[19] To Ěḇer were born two sons: the name of one was Peleḡ, for in his days the earth was divided, and his brother’s name was Yoqtan.
[20] And Yoqtan brought forth <dn>את</dn> Almoḏaḏ, and <dn>את</dn> Sheleph, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥatsarmaveth, and <dn>את</dn> Yeraḥ,
[21] and <dn>את</dn> Haḏoram, and <dn>את</dn> Uzal, and <dn>את</dn> Diqlah,
[22] and <dn>את</dn> Ěyḇal, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇima’ěl, and <dn>את</dn> Sheḇa,
[23] and <dn>את</dn> Ophir, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥavilah, and <dn>את</dn> Yoḇaḇ. All these were the sons of Yoqtan.

readings.title: The Clans of Noah
readings.subtitle: The Nations Spread Abroad
readings.text:
[Genesis 10:31] These were the sons of Shěm, according to their clans, according to their languages, in their lands, according to their nations.
[32] These were the clans of the sons of Noaḥ, according to their generations, in their nations. And from these the nations were divided on the earth after the flood.
